title: Singular & Plural Nouns (-s, -es, irregulars)
description: Learn how to turn singular nouns into plural nouns using regular and irregular rules.
objectives: Convert regular singular nouns to plural by adding -s or -es
Apply spelling rules for words ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, and consonant + y
Identify and use essential irregular plural nouns (child/children, man/men, person/people)

sections.title: Rules for Forming Plural Nouns
sections.content:
A **singular noun** refers to one person, place, or thing. A **plural noun** refers to two or more.

Most English nouns form their plural simply by adding **-s**. However, certain endings require **-es**, spelling alterations, or completely irregular forms.

tables.title: Regular Plural Rules
rows: Standard rule for most English nouns.
Adds an extra syllable /Éªz/ for easy pronunciation.
Drop the y, add -ies. Vowel+y just takes -s (keys, days).

tables.title: Crucial Irregular Plurals
rows: Say 'three people', not 'three persons' in daily speech.

callouts.title: Vowel + Y vs. Consonant + Y
callouts.text: Look at the letter before 'y': if it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u), just add **-s** (boy -> boys, key -> keys). If it is a consonant, change to **-ies** (baby -> babies, story -> stories).

callouts.title: Verb Agreement with Plural Nouns
callouts.text: Plural nouns take plural verbs: 'The child **is** playing' -> 'The children **are** playing'.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Here is what you mastered in this lesson:
summaryPoints: Most nouns become plural by adding -s (book -> books, desk -> desks).
Nouns ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -z add -es (watch -> watches, box -> boxes).
Consonant + y changes to -ies (city -> cities); Vowel + y just adds -s (key -> keys).
Memorize irregular plurals: child -> children, man -> men, woman -> women, person -> people, foot -> feet.
Plural nouns always require plural verbs (e.g. 'The books are...').
